accepted_tls_versions.title: Accepted TLS/SSL Protocol Versions
accepted_tls_versions.description: List of TLS/SSL protocol versions the server is configured to accept (e.g., SSLv3, TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3)

weak_cipher_suites_enabled.title: Weak Cipher Suites Enabled
weak_cipher_suites_enabled.description: Whether the server is configured to accept weak or deprecated cipher suites (e.g., RC4, DES, 3DES, NULL ciphers, EXPORT ciphers, anonymous DH)

certificate_authority_type.title: Certificate Authority Type
certificate_authority_type.description: Indicates whether the TLS certificate is issued by a trusted public CA, a private/internal CA, or is self-signed.

certificate_expired.title: Certificate Expired
certificate_expired.description: Whether the TLS certificate's notAfter date is in the past, making it invalid for client trust validation.

certificate_domain_match.title: Certificate Domain Matches Server Hostname
certificate_domain_match.description: Whether the certificate's Subject CN or Subject Alternative Names (SANs) match the server's configured hostname or public-facing domain.

tls_configured.title: TLS Configured on Server
tls_configured.description: Whether the web server has TLS/HTTPS enabled and a certificate is configured at all.

http_port_open.title: HTTP Port 80 Open
http_port_open.description: Whether the web server is actively listening and accepting connections on port 80 (unencrypted HTTP).

http_to_https_redirect_enabled.title: HTTP to HTTPS Redirect Enabled
http_to_https_redirect_enabled.description: Whether the server is configured to automatically redirect all HTTP (port 80) requests to HTTPS (port 443) with a 301 or 302 redirect response.

hsts_enabled.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) Enabled
hsts_enabled.description: Whether the server sends the Strict-Transport-Security response header, instructing browsers to only communicate over HTTPS.

server_header_disclosure.title: Server Header Discloses Version
server_header_disclosure.description: Indicates whether the HTTP Server response header exposes software name and/or version information (e.g., 'Apache/2.4.51 (Ubuntu)').

x_powered_by_header_disclosure.title: X-Powered-By Header Present
x_powered_by_header_disclosure.description: Indicates whether the X-Powered-By response header is present and exposes technology stack information (e.g., 'PHP/8.0.3', 'Express').

directory_listing_enabled.title: Directory Listing Enabled
directory_listing_enabled.description: Indicates whether the web server is configured to automatically generate and serve directory index pages when no index file is present, allowing clients to enumerate directory contents.

publicly_accessible.title: Publicly Accessible Endpoint
publicly_accessible.description: Indicates whether the web server or the affected virtual host/path is reachable from untrusted networks (e.g., the internet or a shared network), as opposed to being restricted to internal/loopback interfaces only.

authentication_required.title: Authentication Required for Directory Access
authentication_required.description: Indicates whether access to the affected directories or write methods requires authentication, limiting exposure to authenticated users only.

present_security_headers.title: Present Security Response Headers
present_security_headers.description: List of security-relevant HTTP response headers currently present and configured in server responses (e.g., Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy)

hsts_max_age_seconds.title: HSTS max-age Value (Seconds)
hsts_max_age_seconds.description: The max-age directive value from the Strict-Transport-Security header. A value below 31536000 (1 year) is considered insufficient. Use 0 if the header is absent.

csp_policy_configured.title: Content-Security-Policy Configured
csp_policy_configured.description: Whether a non-empty Content-Security-Policy header is present and contains at least a default-src or script-src directive.

allowed_http_methods.title: Allowed HTTP Methods
allowed_http_methods.description: List of HTTP methods the server accepts on the endpoint or globally. Dangerous methods include PUT, DELETE, TRACE, CONNECT.

endpoint_is_static_or_readonly.title: Endpoint Is Static or Read-Only
endpoint_is_static_or_readonly.description: Indicates whether the endpoint is intended to serve only read-only or static content, meaning write/destructive methods should never be permitted.

trace_method_response_reflects_headers.title: TRACE Method Reflects Request Headers
trace_method_response_reflects_headers.description: Indicates whether a TRACE request to the server results in the request body/headers being echoed back, confirming active cross-site tracing (XST) vulnerability.

process_run_uid.title: Web Server Process UID
process_run_uid.description: The numeric user ID (UID) of the OS account running the web server process. UID 0 is root. UIDs below 100 may indicate system or service accounts with elevated access.

process_run_user.title: Web Server Process Run User
process_run_user.description: The OS user account under which the web server process is running (e.g., root, www-data, nginx, apache, nobody)

dedicated_service_account_configured.title: Dedicated Low-Privilege Service Account Configured
dedicated_service_account_configured.description: Whether the web server is explicitly configured to use a dedicated, low-privilege service account (e.g., www-data, nginx, apache) rather than a generic or privileged account.

web_root_owner.title: Web Root Directory Owner
web_root_owner.description: The OS user that owns the web root directory (e.g., /var/www/html). Should be a dedicated web server user, not root or a generic user.

web_root_world_writable.title: Web Root World-Writable
web_root_world_writable.description: Indicates whether the web root directory or its contents have world-writable permissions (mode includes o+w).

config_dir_permissions_octal.title: Web Server Config Directory Permissions (Octal)
config_dir_permissions_octal.description: Octal permission string of the web server configuration directory (e.g., /etc/nginx or /etc/apache2). Safe value is 750 or more restrictive.

access_logging_enabled.title: Access Logging Enabled
access_logging_enabled.description: Whether HTTP access logging is enabled on the web server, capturing requests made to the server.

error_logging_enabled.title: Error Logging Enabled
error_logging_enabled.description: Whether HTTP error logging is enabled on the web server, capturing server errors and anomalous conditions.

log_fields_captured.title: Log Fields Captured
log_fields_captured.description: List of fields captured in the access log format string. Expected fields include: client_ip, request_uri, response_code, timestamp.

log_input_sanitization_enabled.title: Log Input Sanitization Enabled
log_input_sanitization_enabled.description: Whether the server sanitizes or encodes user-supplied input (e.g., newline characters, control characters) before writing it to log files.

logged_user_supplied_fields.title: User-Supplied Fields Written to Logs
logged_user_supplied_fields.description: List of user-controlled HTTP request fields (e.g., User-Agent, Referer, URI, query string, X-Forwarded-For) that are recorded verbatim in server log files.

version_has_known_cve.title: Server Version Has Known CVE
version_has_known_cve.description: Indicates whether the running web server binary or its bundled modules have one or more publicly disclosed CVEs in the current installed version.

days_since_patch_available.title: Days Since Patch Available
days_since_patch_available.description: Number of calendar days elapsed since a patched version addressing the known CVE(s) was publicly released by the vendor, and the server has not yet been updated.

rate_limiting_enabled.title: Rate Limiting Enabled
rate_limiting_enabled.description: Whether per-client or per-IP request rate limiting is configured at the web server or reverse proxy level (e.g., nginx limit_req, Apache mod_ratelimit, or equivalent).

connection_throttling_enabled.title: Connection Throttling Enabled
connection_throttling_enabled.description: Whether limits on simultaneous connections per client or overall concurrent connections are configured (e.g., nginx limit_conn, Apache LimitRequestFields/MaxKeepAliveRequests, or equivalent).

max_request_body_size_bytes.title: Maximum Request Body Size (Bytes)
max_request_body_size_bytes.description: The configured maximum allowed size of an HTTP request body in bytes. A value of 0 or -1 typically indicates no limit is enforced.

default_welcome_page_active.title: Default Welcome Page Active
default_welcome_page_active.description: Whether the server serves its default welcome/index page (e.g., Apache 'It works!', nginx default page, IIS default page) on the root or well-known paths.

sample_scripts_accessible.title: Sample Scripts or Test Endpoints Accessible
sample_scripts_accessible.description: Whether vendor-shipped sample scripts, test pages, or demo endpoints (e.g., /examples/, /cgi-bin/test-cgi, /phpinfo.php, /server-info, /server-status) are reachable and return a 2xx or 3xx response.

vhosts_share_document_root.title: Virtual Hosts Share Document Root
vhosts_share_document_root.description: Indicates whether two or more configured virtual hosts resolve to the same filesystem document root directory, enabling cross-vhost content access.

chroot_or_namespace_isolation_enabled.title: Chroot or Namespace Isolation Enabled
chroot_or_namespace_isolation_enabled.description: Indicates whether each virtual host process or worker runs within a chroot jail, container namespace, or equivalent OS-level isolation boundary preventing cross-vhost filesystem traversal.

path_traversal_controls_enabled.title: Path Traversal Controls Enabled
path_traversal_controls_enabled.description: Indicates whether the server enforces controls that prevent directory traversal sequences (e.g., '../') from escaping the intended document root for each virtual host.

key_file_in_document_root.title: Private Key File Located Within Document Root
key_file_in_document_root.description: Indicates whether any TLS private key file path is located under the web server document root directory, making it potentially retrievable via HTTP request.

key_file_world_readable.title: Private Key File Has World-Readable Permissions
key_file_world_readable.description: Indicates whether the TLS private key file has filesystem permissions that allow reading by users other than the owning user or designated web server group (e.g., mode includes o+r or permissions are 644, 666, 777).
